newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt says no small business rate subsidy.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt says no small business rate subsidy.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Tuesday the government would not subsidise interest rates on loans to small businesses for fear of lulling them into a sense of false security.

"On the finance side, we can offer small businesses very favourable terms but the government will not subsidise interest rates," Erwin told the National African Federated Chamber of Commerce and Industry conference.

The conference, which has as its theme "Partnerships for growth and empowerment", is intended to act as a catalyst to establish strong partnerships between black business, government and major businesses in South Africa.

Erwin told delegates if the government artificially lowered interest rates for small business, it would create "a false base" that would not prepare them for when they had to pay market related interest rates.
The alternative was for the government to fund skills training and provide information to developing small businesses which would make them stronger in the future, he said.
The development of small business was essential to empower previously disadvantaged communities and to give them a stake in the economy, he added.
Erwin said in April that large "world player types" projects should receive tax incentives, as should small business.
He said the latter already had favourable tax treatment in the form of cash-based accounting, which had got off to a difficult start but now looked set to work.
